signature: A 290-floor, 20th-century apartment block with no plan: miles of dim beige plaster halls over laminate and linoleum, identical windowless flats whose fridges refill themselves, stairwells that drop and climb out of sight, lifts that may or may not come, and a lethargy that makes you want to stay.

exits.label: Opened a plain, numberless door; it opened onto Level 0
exits.source_quote: exited to Level 0, Level 114, Level 327, Level 395, or Level 410 by bland and unassuming doors
exits.conditions: Exit doors differ in design from flat doors but are just as drab: flush, painted, no number plate or peephole, a round knob. Anchor (start floor): one plain door on the west hall leads to Level 0. Streamed: about one chunk-storey in six has one, destination seeded.
exits.hint: Not every door in these halls belongs to a flat. Look for one with no number.

exits.source_quote: staircases or elevators on the bottom floor of Level 13 leads to buildings within Level 70 or Level 208

exits.label: Touched a chessboard that the room had set out with two chairs
exits.source_quote: touching the chessboard leads to Level 157
exits.conditions: Streamed only, rare: an empty (uninhabited) flat generates a chessboard on its table between two chairs. Never in inhabited flats; the player cannot arrange furniture, so artificial arrangements cannot occur.
exits.hint: Some empty flats set the table for a game nobody is playing.

exits.label: Tried the door marked 235
exits.source_quote: attempting to open it will teleport you to the level of the same number
exits.conditions: Streamed only, very rare: a flat door whose plate reads 235 (flat plates are floor + two-digit unit, so it stands out).
exits.hint: Read the door numbers. One of them does not follow the pattern.

exits.label: Opened a red door
exits.conditions: Streamed only, rare: a flat door painted red, with no number.
exits.hint: Every door here is brown or beige. Almost every one.

exits.label: Pushed through a wall painted a deeper yellow
exits.source_quote: can lead to Level 289 if noclipped through
exits.conditions: Hold movement into a deeper-yellow wall for about 2.6 s. Anchor: one real yellow wall on the west hall by the stair core and one dud on the north hall. Streamed: rare yellow walls, about 45% real; a dud gives way for a moment and then fails, and after three failures the game tells you it is probably the wrong wall (page: repeated failure means wrong wall).
exits.hint: Some walls are painted a deeper yellow than the rest. Not all of them lead anywhere.

exits.label: Kept climbing a staircase that would not end
exits.source_quote: staircases can change and begin ascending with no end, leading to Level 280
exits.conditions: Streamed only, rare (about one stair core in eleven, never at the start). In such a core the floor numbers stop advancing as you climb; four storeys of climbing past the top of the walkable pair fires the exit. Going down resets it.
exits.hint: If the numbers on the landings stop changing, the stair has stopped going anywhere. Or has it?

entity_policy: No entities spawned and no entity sounds. The page classes the level as Non-Entity Hazards and says there is no evidence for any explanation of the disappearances, so none is shown. Residents are humans who stay in their rooms (page: lethargic, antisocial); this release has no NPC system, so they appear only as traces: shut doors with a doormat and light underneath, a television murmuring through the door, no answer when you knock. Entities named in the Level 808 interview are not on Level 13 and are absent.
notes: SOURCE: apartment-complex look (dull white/beige plaster halls, laminated wood or linoleum, dim light), 290 floors, plentiful stairs with lifts nearby, inconsistent lifts, near-identical flats of a main kitchen-living room + bedroom + bathroom, restocked fridges with basic food and microwavable meals, vintage TV played out of order, old books and clothes, lethargy and attachment to one's room, exits as listed. ADAPTATION: the block grammar is ours (the page gives no map): 24 m chunks, each two halls plus a 22 x 22 m block of three columns of flats around a spine hall, sometimes a cross hall; chunks are randomly transposed (floor-independent) so door-lined strands run both ways and the plan never settles into a grid ('completely unorganised mess'). About 55% of chunks hold a stair core (switchback stair with an open well, lift lobby). The playable world is a finite streaming window (ChunkWorld radius 2, about 6000 colliders) around an infinite seeded plan; the page's 'infinite or looping' extent is never simulated, and halls fade into dim fog instead of ending. ADAPTATION: two storeys are walkable at a time (floor-to-floor 3 m, 2.6 m ceilings, 2.1 m doors, 0.167 m risers). Stair shafts are built two to three floors up and down; climbing past the top of the walkable pair (or below its bottom) moves the pair two floors and re-floors the block around you while you are inside the enclosed stairwell (identical geometry, so the move is seamless). Landing plaques and lift indicators show the floor number (start floor seeded between 21 and 259; floor 1 is the bottom, 290 the top). ADAPTATION: lift call buttons: dead (about 38%), a car passes (20%) or a car comes and jumps 3-60 floors up or down (the ride happens behind a fade; the car interior is not modelled). ADAPTATION: lethargy and attachment are a stateful meter: time in flats, resting, eating and TV raise it; it slows you, removes sprint above 0.65 and drains colour; the first flat you rest in becomes yours and walking away from it drags until the attachment fades. No death and no disappearance mechanic (the page says vanishings affect residents of over a decade and are unexplained). ADAPTATION: flats are either inhabited (door shut, doormat, light under the door, sometimes a TV murmuring; knocking gets no real answer; interior not built) or empty (door open, furnished, enterable). An empty flat's fridge gives one microwaved meal and is restocked 12 s later once you have left and come back. Fridge/TV/bed prompts and knock prompts are created when the player comes close (collider budget). No windows anywhere (the interview describes windowless rooms; testimony). ADAPTATION: light fixtures feed the shadowless light pool per storey (plus stair landings within one storey) so lights do not shine through floors. ADAPTATION: the M.E.G. interview is a paraphrased note in the start flat, marked as testimony; the B.N.T.G. Free Home Project appears only as a paraphrased flyer in the start lift lobby (floor 283 itself is not specially built). The 28/06/22 addendum catastrophe (12% destroyed, 41% damaged) is time-stamped lore and is not built (dossier: leave out of the base build). GAP: Level 387 ('Theoretically, entering any apartment building can lead to Level 387'; RUMORED, scarcely documented) is not built: the level has no apartment buildings to enter from outside. GAP: no arrivals from roster levels (data/canon/transitions.json lists no edge into L013); entrances from Levels 12, 21, 62, 151, 210, 215, 683, 979 and 2-FR await those levels. GAP: lifts at the bottom floor do not lead out (stairs only).
